core_obligations: Choose a presentation of the space, let the inverse image of the closed subset in each member be the corresponding closed subset, and use the base change identity for completions to obtain a presentation of the completion (proof lines 8166-8172).

Show that quasi-compactness of the complement of the closed subset passes to the complements of the inverse images, and that local countable indexedness, the local adic* property and local Noetherianness each pass to the members (proof lines 8172-8177).
Conclude the three statements by the affine case (proof lines 8177-8179).
proof_roadmap: Presentation of the completion and the base change identity (proof lines 8166-8172).
Transfer of the hypotheses to the members (proof lines 8172-8177).
Conclusion by the affine case (proof lines 8177-8179).
difficulty_reason: For a formal algebraic space X and a closed subset T of its reduction, the lemma asserts that the completion of X along T is locally countably indexed, locally adic* and locally Noetherian under the corresponding hypotheses on X, with the additional assumption that the complement of T maps quasi-compactly to the reduction in the first two cases (statement lines 8151-8164). The proof reduces all three statements to the affine case by choosing a presentation of X: the inverse image of T in each member is a closed subset, the base change of the completion along the member is the completion of the member along that subset, and these base changes form a presentation of the completion (proof lines 8166-8172). It then checks that the hypotheses transfer to the members: quasi-compactness of the complement passes to the complement of the inverse image, and the three properties of X pass to the members (proof lines 8172-8179). The conclusion is the affine statement proved earlier (proof lines 8177-8179). The claim is H2: the reduction is carried out by a presentation and a base change identity, the transfer of each hypothesis is stated, and the three cases are then settled by one named affine result.
